name: Central Maui Boxing Club
ages: Reach out to the club to find the right age group for your child.
description: A nonprofit youth-development club founded in 1993, building discipline, respect and confidence through coached boxing. The club hosts sanctioned amateur competition; its athlete Faith Kahula Boteilho earned national bronze in 2026.
where: Reach out to the club for the gym address and training times. Competition bouts are held at separate venues.
season: The club trains year-round. Contact the coach for this season’s schedule.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Ask about beginner instruction, protective gear, medical requirements and readiness for sparring. A sanctioned bout requires the club’s approval and USA Boxing participation requirements.

name: Southside Boxing Club of Maui
ages: Club materials describe youth from age 6
description: A community nonprofit led by Nante Manangan, pairing boxing fundamentals with mentoring and character development. Southside boxer Micah Diaz won a 2026 Junior Olympics national title.
where: Kīhei. Contact the club for the training location.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
contact: Nante Manangan · official website contact route
extra: The club describes a donation-supported free youth mission. Ask which training, equipment and travel costs are currently covered; assistance is not a guarantee of a place or a universally free package.

name: Aloha Archers / Maui Hunters And Sportsmens
ages: Contact the club for youth program availability.
description: An NFAA archery club with outdoor and 3D ranges on a private ranch. Seabury Hall’s archery team trains here. Contact the club to arrange youth lessons.
registration: Contact the club about youth lessons, membership, equipment and range access.

name: Aloft Archers
ages: Parent–youth teams. Contact the program for age details.
description: A family outdoor-skills program connecting archery and bowhunting with safety, conservation, field skills and parent–child communication. This is distinct from a target-archery tournament club.
where: Workshops are held across Hawaiʻi. Contact Aloft about the next one in Maui County.
registration: Contact Aloft about the next local session, parent participation, equipment, fees and scholarships.

name: Lānaʻi Parks & Recreation Youth Archery
ages: Ask the district about age groups
description: County youth archery on Lānaʻi. Contact recreation staff about classes and how to join.
registration: Ask the district whether sessions are running this term, and about ages, dates, equipment and registration. The directory does not establish that enrollment is open.

name: Four Seasons Resort Lānaʻi Archery
description: A commercial guided lesson with bows, arrows and instruction included. The upland range experience is separate from a community youth club or school team.
registration: Reserve through the resort. Staff can help with resident and guest options, rates and sessions.
extra: Published child pricing for ages 9–12 was $90. Confirm the current rate before booking; transportation and other inclusions are described by the resort.

name: One Love Skate
ages: Contact the program about ages, waivers and group size.
description: Faith-based skateboarding instruction and mentorship through weekly Acts 4:20 groups, community partnerships, camps and skate jams. Coached groups are distinct from independent use of public skateparks.
where: Pukalani Skatepark and Pāʻia Youth & Cultural Center.
season: Pukalani on Thursdays: gather at 4:20 p.m., practice 4:30–5:30 p.m. A Pāʻia group also meets Thursdays; contact the organizers for details.
registration: Contact the coaches before your first session about dates, ages, waivers, equipment and openings.
extra: Kīhei, Hāna, Lahaina and Keōpūolani are not active weekly One Love groups. Pop-up events at those parks are separate. The September 26, 2026 Pukalani Skate Jam was suspended; a new date hasn’t been announced.

name: Pāʻia Youth & Cultural Center / StoneWave
description: A youth center with a skatepark, in partnership with One Love. Center membership is free; StoneWave skating has its own pass fees and waiver.
season: Tuesday–Saturday, 2–6:30 p.m. (closed in bad weather).
registration: Contact PYCC for membership, skatepark waivers, pass prices and hours.
extra: Helmets and shoes required. Published skate passes: $5 daily, $15 monthly, $150 yearly. Under-9 and over-19 users have separate waiver requirements. Old 2018 Skate School camps are not current offerings.

name: Mana Mentors
ages: Ages vary by event. Contact the program for details.
description: A West Maui nonprofit connecting youth mentorship, surf/skate recreation and community events. It supported Lahaina Skate Park’s reopening and mobile skate-jam access.
where: West Maui. Locations vary by activity.
registration: Contact the program about youth skate activities and how to join.

name: Duke Maliu Skate Park
ages: Public recreation; supervision is the family’s responsibility
description: A County skatepark with wooden ramps, platforms, stairs and rails. Park access does not include an organized lesson or youth league.
season: Open daily 7 a.m.–10 p.m. (County hours).
registration: Free public park. Bring a helmet and pads, and check County park rules before you go.

name: Maui Rugby
description: Maui’s home for youth rugby: recreational and competitive play, Maui Cup sevens, Hawaiʻi Youth Rugby and travel teams. Rookie rugby is noncontact.
season: Maui Cup runs January–March, and high-school and travel play runs February–August.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: USA Rugby/Rugby Xplorer membership is separate from any club dues or subsidies. Do not assume the older 2025–26 registration notice applies to 2026–27.

name: Kahului Rugby Warriors
description: A regional Maui Rugby team describing free recreational rugby and competitive opportunities in Hawaiʻi and beyond. Beginner/noncontact and tackle placement depend on the child’s age and experience.
registration: Contact the club to sign up. They can share the practice location, age divisions and membership costs.

name: Na Pueo Rugby
ages: Contact the program to find the right division.
description: A Maui club in Hawaiʻi Youth Rugby. Contact the club about teams and how to join.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Maui Wahine
ages: Girls’ youth pathway. Contact the club for age groups.
description: A girls rugby program with players on the 2026 USA Rugby U18 women’s development roster. Contact Maui Rugby about joining.
registration: Contact Maui Rugby to be connected with Maui Wahine. They can share ages, practice location, registration and fees.

name: 808 Gymnastics
description: Recreational gymnastics, tumbling and a USA Gymnastics competitive team. Classes use floor, bars, beam, vault, tumble track and trampoline.
season: Regular classes and seasonal school-break camps.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Published monthly tuition: $90 parent–child/preschool, $95 one regular class weekly, $155 two weekly; $30 annual administration fee and 10% sibling discount. Prices can change, so check with the program.

name: Island Athletics Maui
ages: Programs begin at age 1; school-age and camp groups vary
description: Year-round recreational gymnastics, Parent & Tot, preschool movement, tumbling, ninja tumbling and seasonal camps. The larger Kahului facility opened in 2026.
season: Year-round classes; dated camps announced separately.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: A USA Gymnastics competition team is not established by these listings; ask about the appropriate recreational class.

name: Maui Tumblers
description: Mobile, noncompetitive gymnastics with after-school classes, private and small-group lessons, and skill workshops. Some classes are held at schools for their students.
season: 2026–27 school-year classes.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
contact: Melissa Rajesh / Anuhea Doran · program office
extra: Maui public-site offerings include Makawao, Kula and Pukalani Elementary, Haʻikū community classes and Seabury grades 3–8. Carden, Montessori and Nā Pua O Kula classes are student-only. Molokaʻi offerings include Kaunakakai and Kilohana Elementary and Nā Kamaliʻi Hoaloha Preschool. Published monthly rates: Maui Pre-K $58 + GET / elementary $75 + GET; Molokaʻi $55 / $72; sibling discount 10%.

name: Maui Inline Hockey Association
ages: Youth league. Contact the league for this season’s divisions.
description: Inline hockey at Kalama Park with youth practices and league games. Players register with AAU first, then with the league. Financial help is available.
where: Kalama Park inline rink, 1900 S. Kīhei Rd.
season: 2026–27 registration opened August 15. Youth hockey runs Monday–Thursday at 5 p.m.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Public skating Friday/Saturday 5–9 p.m. is general skating, not hockey instruction. Bring your own skates to skate free; rentals are listed at $10. Ask about hockey fees, beginner skills, protective gear and loaners.

name: Hawaii All-Stars
description: Beginner and all-star cheer, tumbling, stunts, jumps, conditioning and private instruction. Competition teams have placement and travel commitments distinct from introductory training.
season: 2026–27 team program. Contact the gym about placement.
registration: Contact the program about beginner classes, placement, tuition, uniforms and competitions.

name: Maui Pop Warner Cheer & Dance
ages: Contact the program about cheer age groups and squads.
description: Youth cheer and dance through Maui Pop Warner. Teams are based on where you live. Contact the federation to see which districts have cheer and whether it’s sideline, competitive or both.
registration: Contact the federation about cheer registration, fees, uniforms, practices and openings.

name: Valley Isle Road Runners Youth Program
ages: Youth cross country K–8; student membership through 17
description: A community running nonprofit with a youth cross-country series: half-mile K–1 and 2–3, one mile grades 4–5, and 1.5 miles grades 6–8. School teams and unattached runners can participate.
registration: Contact the club for upcoming series dates. Registration is on Athletic.net.
extra: Youth series participation is described as free; separate keiki/student club membership is $20/year. General adult group runs have separate supervision and age questions.

name: Healthy Kids Running Series Maui
description: Five weekly age-appropriate running events from short dashes through one mile, with a Challenger Division. This is a beginner running series rather than a school cross-country team or full track-and-field program.
season: Fall 2026: October 18, 25; November 1, 8, 15, 4–5 p.m.
registration: Register through the organizer. The full series has been $54 including fees, or $16.90 for a single day.

name: Evolution Dance Academy
description: Ballet, contemporary, hip-hop, jazz, tap and acro through studio technique and youth crews. Evolution is MAPA’s resident dance-training partner, rather than a second duplicate MAPA dance school.
season: 2026–27 season.
registration: Contact the studio about class placement and openings. Performance crews are by audition.

name: Momentum Dance Maui
description: Recreational and full-time dance in ballet, jazz, contemporary, hip-hop and tap. Full-time dancers may audition for Nutcracker and Competition Company opportunities.
season: Fall 2026 classes; future camps announced separately.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Kīhei Dance Connection
ages: Intro Hula 5–14; other age groups vary by class
description: Keiki Polynesian/hula and studio dance, including creative movement, ballet/tap, jazz/hip-hop, lyrical and acro. Intro Hula includes Hawaiian language and cultural context.
season: 2026–27 keiki program.
registration: Contact the studio about levels, tuition and openings. Trial classes are offered when space allows.

name: Alexander Academy of Performing Arts
ages: Creative movement, youth and teen levels
description: Ballet and broader dance education with a nonprofit performance company. Youth performance and intensive placement depends on age, training and auditions.
where: 275 W. Kaʻahumanu Ave. #C102, Kahului, plus satellite locations.
season: Fall 2026 classes; seasonal productions and intensives.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Contact the academy for the class appropriate to your child and the current schedule at each location.

name: Hālau Hula Malani O Kapehe
description: Traditional kahiko and ʻauana hula with weekly classes; the hālau also describes Tahitian for keiki.
where: Hale Mahaolu Elima community hall, 11 Mahaolu St.
registration: The hālau isn’t taking new students right now. Ask to join the waitlist.

name: Hālau Keʻalaokamaile
ages: Contact the hālau for youth program availability.
description: Hawaiian cultural education rooted in hula, language, tradition and land-based learning under Kumu Kealiʻi Reichel. Youth performance history does not establish open keiki enrollment.
registration: Contact the hālau about openings, age groups and class location.

name: Lānaʻi Academy of Performing Arts
description: Youth performing arts with 6–8 week sessions in dance, acting and music planned for 2026–27. Contact LAPA about upcoming dance sessions.
registration: Contact LAPA about dance classes, ages, session dates, fees and openings.

name: Liliʻuokalani Trust Hoʻokanaka
description: A Hawaiian cultural youth program including hula, oli, fishing, canoe paddling, storytelling and mālama ʻāina. It is a broader cultural program rather than a standalone dance studio.
season: 2026 program: monthly Fridays, March 20–December 18, plus a June camp.
registration: Use the Trust program contact route for eligibility, next meeting and participation requirements.

name: Maui OnStage Education
description: Musical-theatre classes combine dance/movement, music and drama, including introductory tap for Broadway Kids. This is a related performance pathway rather than a standalone dance school.
season: Fall youth session August 10–December 18, 2026.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Maui Junior Golf Association
ages: Junior age divisions. The coach will help place your child.
description: Junior golf development, tournaments, rules, etiquette, sportsmanship and financial access. The 2026 championship included age divisions from 8 & Under through 15–18.
where: Tournaments at courses around Maui. Mailing address: P.O. Box 852, Wailuku.
registration: 2026 membership is closed. Contact the association about next season.

name: Lahaina Junior Golf Association
ages: Junior golfers. Contact the program to see if your child is eligible.
description: Tournament participation, course discounts and mentorship, with event scholarship and college-assistance opportunities supporting Maui youth.
registration: Contact the association about membership, ages, tournaments and financial help.

name: HSJGA / First Tee Hawaiʻi — Maui
description: A junior golf development and tournament pathway with Maui events. Fall PGA Jr. League combines skill practice with on-course match play at Wailea Blue and Gold/Emerald.
season: Published five-week Maui program October–November 2026.
registration: Contact HSJGA about openings, schedules and need-based scholarships.
extra: Association tournament participation and PGA Jr. League enrollment are separate offerings.

name: Manele Golf Course Junior Instruction
description: Commercial junior instruction and family golf with equipment support. Junior play after noon is described as complimentary for ages 17 and under when accompanied by a paying adult.
registration: Reserve through the resort. Staff can explain resident and guest options and lesson rates.
extra: Published junior lesson inclusions: clubs, shoes, range use and balls.

name: Maui Nui Golf Club / Da Nui Academy
description: Individual and group junior coaching, including Renee Lee’s PGA/US Kids development experience. Family-play access is separate from a coached class.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Published junior instruction with Renee Lee was $80/hour. Junior play ages 17 and under was $29 before 3 p.m., free after 3 p.m. with a paying adult. Prices can change, so check with the program.

name: The Dunes at Maui Lani
description: PGA instruction and junior development with individual/group learning and school/college goals. Dated clinics are separate from permanent coaching.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Wailea Golf Academy
description: Private junior lessons with junior and kamaʻāina rates. Contact the academy for suitable instruction and equipment needs.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Upcountry AYSO Region 818
description: Recreational soccer serving Haʻikū, Kula, Makawao, Pāʻia and Pukalani families. Age division is determined by the season’s birth-date chart.
season: Fall 2026: August–mid-November.
registration: Contact the region about openings and the next registration. Season fees have been $90 early (including the national fee) and $120 regular.

name: Keiki Soccer Pros
description: Beginner-friendly classes with movement, ball skills and fun games in Central, South and West Maui. Registered kids ages 5–11 can join optional scrimmages.
season: Fall/Winter 2026 seasonal classes.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Many listed sessions are $139–$159; price and availability depend on location and session. A girls 6–8 class is listed at Keōpūolani. School enrichment may have student-only access.

name: ALBION SC Hawaii — Maui
description: Developmental academy and competitive soccer, plus MLS GO recreational programs. Formerly Maui United.
where: Central Maui Regional Sports Complex and program-specific fields.
season: Seasonal Keiki/Juniors blocks and 2026–27 teams.
registration: Contact the club to find the right age program and openings. Fall Keiki Academy is full, and holiday program dates are estimates.
extra: Keiki Academy equipment: cleats, socks, shin guards, size-three ball and ALBION training kit.

name: Excel Soccer Academy
description: Low-pressure development through the Farm, then academy/competitive progression, camps and targeted clinics. Farm serves girls and boys.
registration: 2026–27 tryouts are done. Contact the director about an evaluation or Farm team openings.

name: Maui Strikers Soccer Club
ages: Girls and boys; placement by birth year
description: A youth soccer club with development and competitive teams. Contact the club to find the right team for your child.
where: Eddie Tam Lower Fields and Central Maui fields. Your coach will share the practice site.
registration: Use the club’s new-family contact to ask about team placement and openings.

name: Valley Isle Soccer Academy
ages: Youth player development. Contact the club for age groups.
description: HYSA-listed academy offering competitive development, specialty clinics and individual/small-group coaching.
registration: Contact the club about programs, tuition, evaluations and training fields.

name: FA Maui
ages: Contact the club about this season’s youth teams.
description: A Maui youth soccer club. Contact the club about birth-year teams, coaches and practices.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Maui FC
description: A competitive club connected with Keiki Soccer Pros’ advanced-player pathway. Fall travel-club training is listed at Kahului Community Park.
registration: Contact the club about age groups, evaluations, tuition and travel. Full-season training has been $300.

name: Molokaʻi AYSO Region 985
description: Coed recreational soccer with balanced teams and uniforms provided. Families bring shin guards and cleats. Coaches set practice times.
where: Kaunakakai Soccer Field and district practice fields.
season: Spring generally February–April; Fall Saturday games.
registration: Contact the league for next season’s dates and fees.

name: Valley Isle Softball Little League
ages: Ages 4–16. Contact the program for this season’s divisions.
description: A girls softball league welcoming beginners, with development toward Little League Major and Junior All-Stars. Its first season opened in January 2026 with 17 teams.
where: Central Maui Regional Sports Complex, Kahului School fields and Papohaku. Your coach will share your team’s field.
season: The first season began January 17, 2026. Contact the league about the next one.
registration: Contact the league about registration, age divisions, equipment and fees. Need-based scholarships have been offered.
extra: Instagram @ValleyIsleSBLL. Maui Girls Softball Association supported formation of VISLL.

name: Phase 1 / Maui Sports Leagues
description: Structured 5v5 youth flag football with coed and girls-only divisions. Divisions differ between seasonal sessions.
where: Central Maui Regional Sports Complex, Kahului · Fall listing.
season: Fall 2026: October 17–December 12.
registration: Late registration runs October 1–24 for $140. A team coach must approve your child before you register.

name: Molokaʻi County Youth Flag Football
description: Free County Parks & Recreation youth league, separate from high-school girls flag football. Inclusion support is available through the County.
season: September 21–November 24, 2026.
registration: Registration ran August 10–September 14. Contact recreation staff about late openings or next season.

name: Maui Pop Warner Federation
ages: Youth tackle football. Contact the program to see which age divisions play locally.
description: Community tackle football organized through local Maui districts. Players are assigned according to their physical home address.
season: Fall football. Contact the federation for the team calendar.
registration: Signup for this season has closed. Contact the federation about openings or next season.
extra: Published football fees: $65 7U/Tiny Mites; $95 other divisions. Bring two residency proofs, birth certificate, consent/medical forms; report card and contracts are also required. National age divisions do not establish every locally fielded division.

name: Maui Family YMCA Aquatics
ages: Lessons 6 months+ · youth swim club 5+ with prerequisites
description: Progressive water comfort, safety and stroke lessons, private instruction and a noncompetitive Youth Swim Club emphasizing technique, speed and endurance.
season: Lessons run in two-month sessions. Contact the Y to sign up for the next one.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Youth Swim Club requires Level 3 stamina and a 50-yard lap of front and back crawl. Published private package: six 45-minute lessons $147 member/$294 nonmember; learn-to-swim four 30-minute lessons $89/$178. Prices can change, so check with the program.

name: County of Maui Aquatics
ages: Youth lessons vary by pool and session
description: Learn-to-swim, water safety and school swim programs, including School to Pool for participating schools.
registration: Contact the County Aquatics Section for lesson schedules, ages and registration. Daily pool-status line: 808-270-8208.
extra: Swimming and diving are different skills. Ask specifically about supervised diving instruction; boards at a pool do not establish a youth competition team.

name: Island Aquatics
description: A MAGSA/USA Swimming club with beginner-to-advanced development and open-water competition. Team placement depends on assessment and openings.
registration: Contact the club about lessons, team tryouts, openings, USA Swimming membership and costs.

name: Maui Dolphins Swim Club
description: Intro to Swim Team and year-round competitive swimming, with published competitive practice operations on all three islands. Neighbor-island groups have separate local arrangements.
where: Upcountry Aquatic Center, 90 Pukalani St. Contact the program for Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi locations.
season: Short course September–February; long course March–August.
registration: Competitive team enrollment is closed for now. Intro sessions run every so often, usually 6–8 weeks. Contact the club about the next one.
extra: Intro swimmers must be comfortable in 3.5–4 feet, swim one length and submerge/blow bubbles. Published competitive dues $600/season, additional sibling $500, 2026 USA Swimming $90. Prices can change, so check with the program.

name: Lahaina Swim Club
description: Learn-to-swim and competitive USA Swimming groups with swimmer evaluation and small new-swimmer groups.
season: Published Fall 2026 groups August 1–December 30.
registration: Fall groups are full. Contact the club about evaluations and the waitlist.
contact: Jack Pope · head coach / evaluation contact
extra: Published USA Swimming membership: $90 Premier / $30 Flex. Ask which membership and club fee apply.

name: Maui Swim Club
description: A competitive MAGSA swim club with long ties to the Coach Sakamoto Invitational.
registration: Use MAGSA’s team contact to ask about coaches, age groups, tryouts and dues.

name: Hawaii Swim Club — Maui
description: A MAGSA and USA Swimming club on Maui. The local team handles groups, tryouts and enrollment.
registration: Use MAGSA’s club contact to ask about youth groups, coaches and fees.

name: Special Olympics Hawaiʻi Swimming
description: Adaptive competitive swimming with individual and relay events. Contact the program about the local training group and eligibility.
registration: Contact Special Olympics for Maui-area assessment, eligibility, local coach, training schedule and registration.

name: Maui Community Tennis Organization / USTA
description: Junior team leagues, tournaments and red/orange/green ball development. Beginners play with kid-sized balls in groups by level.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Maui Junior Tennis Grant: residents 18 and under with financial need may apply for up to $500 toward approved tournament travel. Ask about current grant rules.

name: Royal Lahaina Tennis Ranch
description: A USTA junior tennis center with private lessons, clinics and junior tournaments. Groups have included Green Ball (8–10), Yellow Ball (11–13) and Varsity Prep (14–18).
registration: Contact the facility about junior clinics, lessons and resident pricing.
extra: Published resident private lessons: $50/30 minutes, $90/hour; semi-private $130/hour for 2–4 players. Prices can change, so check with the program.

name: Wailea Tennis Club
description: Junior tennis, private and semi-private coaching, and court access. Contact the club about junior class ages and nonmember signup.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Published resident court rate $17/player/day with Hawaiʻi ID; standard $30; racquet rental $10. Court fees are separate from instruction.

name: Kapalua Tennis Garden
ages: Family and junior play. Contact the facility for lesson ages.
description: Year-round tennis lessons, private coaching and family court time.
registration: Reserve through the tennis facility. Staff can help with junior lessons, family play and prices.

name: Four Seasons Resort Lānaʻi Junior Tennis
description: A 90-minute junior lesson emphasizing strokes and game play, plus private instruction. This is a commercial resort program with separate guest/local access rules.
registration: Contact the resort about resident and guest options, session times and rates.

name: Maui Surfer Girls
description: Coed youth and family lessons with gear included, plus teen girls camps. Kids need to be comfortable swimmers.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.
extra: Published two-hour private lesson starts at $225, group at $115. Teen camp ages 13–17 is seasonal; the 2026 Camp Olowalu sessions are past. Ask about current resident rates and scholarships.

name: Mana O Maui Surf-N-Turf
description: Free after-school surfing/outdoor mentorship with transportation, gear and food. Activities combine ocean safety, teamwork and stewardship, with hikes when surf conditions are unsuitable.
season: Published September 2026 Wednesday sessions are past.
registration: Contact the program about the next session and openings.
extra: Published group capacity 12; Central Maui pickup points included Boys & Girls Club and ʻĪao School.

name: Surf Club Maui
ages: Kids camps 10–15; youth lessons by arrangement
description: Youth lessons and seasonal three-day kids camps with equipment and coached ocean learning.
where: 1900 S. Kīhei Rd. Your instructor will confirm the exact meeting spot.
registration: Book a lesson anytime, or contact the school about the next camp.

name: Got’um Surfing
ages: Keiki programs. Contact the program for lesson ages.
description: Native Hawaiian-owned surf school with keiki sessions and coached lessons. Meeting locations and conditions are confirmed by instructors.
season: Published October Sesh dates October 5, 6, 8 and 9, 2026, 8–10 a.m.
registration: Contact the school about October openings or the next keiki session. Four days have been $276, or $117 for a single day.

name: Maui Vibe Surf Club
description: Private/group surf lessons and kids camp instruction. This is a commercial lesson pathway rather than a standing competitive club.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Maui WaveRiders
description: Private and semi-private youth surf lessons, matched to your child’s age, ability and the day’s conditions.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: LahAina Surf Shack
ages: School programs grades 1–6; youth lesson rules vary
description: Operating after the Lahaina fire with youth/family lessons, advertised after-school surfing and summer camps. Younger children generally need private instruction.
registration: Contact the program about the meeting location, after-school schedule and openings. Children 8 and under usually take private lessons.

name: Maui Surf Clinics
description: A youth-eligible commercial surf school emphasizing water-safety-trained instructors and beginner lessons.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Surf Yoga Maui
description: Personalized two-hour family/beginner surf instruction at Kalama Park.
registration: Contact the school about ages, lesson types and booking.

name: Hawaiian Paddle Sports Surf Lessons
description: Private guided surf lessons with the meeting point selected for conditions. Surf instruction is separate from canoe programs.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Hawaiʻi Surfing Association Maui
ages: Junior and amateur divisions. Contact the program for age groups.
description: Local competition and state advancement through HSA Maui / Maui Surf Ohana. Contest entry and season membership are separate steps.
registration: Contest dates, divisions, fees and entry deadlines are posted on HSA’s LiveHeats page.

name: Adaptive Maui / Kelea Foundation
ages: Contact the program to see if your child is eligible.
description: Adaptive surfing and accessible beach days. Talk with the team about your child’s needs before booking.
registration: Contact the program to sign up. They can tell you about age groups, openings, fees and practice times.

name: Maui Juniors Volleyball Club
description: Fundamental and tactical training for boys and girls, with local, regional and national competition. Team registration and tryouts vary by group.
registration: Contact the club about tryouts, team fees, gyms and travel. Spots are limited.

name: Kahālāwai Volleyball Club
description: West Maui youth volleyball instruction for girls and boys, including serving, passing, attacking, defense and game development.
where: West Maui. The 2026 preseason camp was held at Maui Prep’s Bozich Center.
registration: Contact the club about the next camp and team openings.

name: Nakamura Wrestling
